newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's KI sees 1997 GDP 2.0 pct, 1998 3.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's KI sees 1997 GDP 2.0 pct, 1998 3.0 pct.

text.p: Sweden's National Institute of Economic Research KI forecast on Monday that Swedish Gross Domestic Product (GDP) would rise two percent in 1997 and three percent in 1998.
The institute said it expected consumer prices to rise 0.9 percent this year and 1.5 percent in 1998.
KI showed some revisions from its March forecast when it saw CPI rising 0.5 percent this year and 1.5 percent in 1998, while it expected GDP to increase two percent in 1997 and 2.5 percent in 1998.
KI said it appeared difficult for the Swedish government to reach its target of halving unemployment to four percent by the year 2000.
It expected unemployment of 8.5 percent in 1997 and to 7.7 percent in 1998 compared to a May 1997 level of 7.8 percent.

"The economic upturn is strengthening gradually," KI said. "After a certain levelling off during the past half year KI forecast in its June report faster growth in the second half of 1997 and in 1998."
Despite the upturn it expected inflation in 1997 and 1998 to remain below the central bank target of two percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side.
It forecast that current account surpluses would increase somewhat this year and in 1998.
"A softer Swedish crown and fast productivity growth means an improved competitive situation for the Swedish export industry compared to the situation in 1996," KI said.
"Rising prices on forestry products and falling oil prices contribute to the strengthening of the current account."
